name: infra_lightning_cli
title: Lightning project: LightningModule + LightningDataModule + callbacks + LightningCLI + YAML
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the full Lightning project shape, CLI and config included
note: One planted defect (MLV711) on an otherwise correct project. The datamodule is the precision trap: the split runs first and the scaler is fitted on the training partition only, so MLV101 and MLV102 must both stay silent even though a StandardScaler and a train_test_split sit four lines apart.
stagesObserved: config, data, preprocess, model, objective, train, eval present; `deliver` is reported absent although ModelCheckpoint(monitor="val/loss", ...) is registered at cli.py line 34 - see the domain-infra report, finding INFRA-04.

expected.defect: configure_optimizers returns ([optimizer], [scheduler]) with a OneCycleLR and no {"interval": "step"}
expected.why: Lightning steps a scheduler returned that way once per epoch, so the whole one-cycle schedule finishes in the first few epochs and the remaining 25 train at the floor learning rate - silently, because nothing raises

forbidden.why: train_test_split runs at lines 46 and 49 and the scaler is only FITTED at line 53, on x_train; the validation and test matrices are merely transformed at lines 55-56
self.scaler.transform (not fit / fit_transform) is what touches x_val and x_test
there is no cross-validation call in this project
the training loader is built with shuffle=True at line 69
the val and test loaders are both built with shuffle=False at lines 74 and 78
num_workers is a constructor argument of the DataModule, and Lightning - not this module - owns the process start method; the CLI entrypoint carries the __main__ guard
there is no hand-written loop: training_step returns the loss and Lightning owns zero_grad / backward / step
validation_step is a Lightning hook; the framework switches the module to eval() and wraps the hook in no_grad itself
same: Lightning runs validation_step and test_step under torch.no_grad()
forward returns self.head(self.backbone(x)) - raw logits, with no softmax anywhere - and F.cross_entropy is fed exactly that
Lightning owns device placement for both the module and the batches
seed_everything(1234, workers=True) is called at cli.py line 46, both train_test_split calls pass random_state=self.seed, and configs/fit.yaml sets seed_everything: 1234
both train_test_split calls pass random_state=self.seed (lines 48 and 50)
ConversionClassifier.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 27
ConversionDataModule.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement at line 28
the backbone is an nn.Sequential and the two metrics are torchmetrics modules assigned directly; there is no plain list of submodules
training_step contains no .backward() and no optimizer .step(); it returns the loss and lets Lightning apply it
training_step returns the loss at line 54
